note: Generic, per-tier housing/farming-system photos, reused across every brand assigned that tier -- never depicts a specific company's facility. Real photo sourced first per housing-imagery.md's process; AI generation only as a fallback when no genuinely free, clearly-licensed, non-advocacy real photo existed.

grass-finished-beef.jpg.depicts: Cattle grazing on pasture, USDA's own illustration of the organic/grass-fed grazing concept. Not tied to any company in the catalog.

conventional-beef-feedlot.jpg.author: Wikimedia user H20
conventional-beef-feedlot.jpg.depicts: Generic cattle feedlot, Texas Panhandle. Not tied to any specific named company.

crate-free-pork.jpg.author: Wikimedia user Hajotthu
crate-free-pork.jpg.depicts: Free-range sow with piglets, Bonstorf, Germany -- illustrates group/open housing (absence of individual gestation crates), not tied to any company in the catalog.

gestation-crate.png.reason: No usable real photo found. The only real candidate on Wikimedia Commons ('Gestation crates 2.jpg') depicts a NAMED Smithfield Foods/Murphy Brown facility -- Smithfield is one of the 8 companies in this catalog's meat-poultry module, so using it would both violate the 'never depict a specific company's facility' rule AND directly implicate a real sourced company from advocacy-photography content. Same structural gap as eggs' cage-free/aviary tier: this is a heavily advocacy-photographed welfare topic with no neutral, freely-licensed alternative.

wild-caught.jpg.author: C. Ortiz Rojas, NOAA
wild-caught.jpg.depicts: Commercial purse-seine catch (Chilean jack mackerel, not tuna specifically) -- illustrates the GENERIC wild-caught commercial fishing practice, not a species- or company-specific claim. All 3 tuna companies in the catalog (StarKist, Bumble Bee, Wild Planet) are wild-caught; no real, clearly-licensed, non-advocacy tuna-specific purse-seine photo was found in the time spent searching.

farmed.jpg.author: Wikimedia user Vebra (originally posted to Panoramio)
farmed.jpg.depicts: Generic shrimp aquaculture pond, Madura, Indonesia. Not tied to Rich Products/SeaPak or any other company in the catalog -- SeaPak's own actual farming country is unconfirmed (see companies.js sourcing.welfareSeafood.farmingCountry: 'unknown'), so this image is deliberately generic rather than implying a specific country match.
